evidenceAudit.scope: Women considering hysterectomy for benign disease (usually heavy menstrual bleeding or fibroids): investigation, alternatives, consent, major-surgery tests, VTE and antibiotic prophylaxis. Verified against NICE NG88, NG45 (total abdominal hysterectomy = major surgery), NG89 and Saudi MOH Protocol-015.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Route of hysterectomy (vaginal/laparoscopic/abdominal) selection not covered
SFDA registration not checked per drug
Local antibiogram may add gentamicin (MOH p. 1)

pathophysiology.summary: Hysterectomy removes the uterus and ends menstruation and fertility. For benign disease it is offered when less invasive treatments are unsuitable or have failed, after full discussion of implications.
keyMechanisms: Fibroids, adenomyosis and endometrial pathology cause heavy bleeding and pressure symptoms.
Chronic blood loss leads to iron-deficiency anaemia — check FBC (NICE NG88).
Fibroids increase the risk of serious operative complications such as haemorrhage and organ damage (NICE NG88).

symptoms: Heavy menstrual bleeding affecting quality of life.
Pelvic pain, pressure symptoms, intermenstrual bleeding.
physicalSigns: Enlarged or irregular uterus on examination.
redFlags: Postmenopausal or persistent intermenstrual bleeding — exclude malignancy

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Risk factors; hysteroscopy and biopsy (NICE NG88).

clinicalManagement.title: Alternatives and consent
actions: Discuss LNG-IUS, medical treatment, endometrial ablation, myomectomy or uterine artery embolisation where suitable (NICE NG88).
Full discussion of hysterectomy implications, including fertility loss and higher complication risk with fibroids (NICE NG88).

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-operative assessment
actions: Grade surgery (minor, intermediate, major/complex) and ASA status; order only the tests NICE NG45 lists for that combination.
Do not routinely order chest X-ray, urine dipstick, sickle tests or HbA1c in people without diabetes (NICE NG45).
Discuss stopping smoking and reducing alcohol; manage iron-deficiency anaemia (NICE NG180).
Make an individual anticoagulant plan if the person takes anticoagulants (NICE NG45).

clinicalManagement.title: VTE prophylaxis
actions: Mechanical prophylaxis from admission (stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression) until mobility returns (NICE NG89 1.14.2).
Add LMWH (or fondaparinux) for at least 7 days if VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk (NICE NG89 1.14.3) — enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily (FDA label).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH Protocol-015)
actions: Vaginal or abdominal hysterectomy: cefazolin 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min of incision (MOH p. 1).
Allergy: clindamycin 900 mg IV plus gentamicin 5 mg/kg single dose within 60 min (MOH p. 1).
Re-dose cefazolin every 4 h (or clindamycin every 6 h) if surgery lasts more than 4 h or blood loss exceeds 1,500 mL (MOH p. 1).
Stop prophylaxis within 24 h of the end of surgery, even with drains or catheters (MOH p. 4).

keyPoints: Major surgery tests: FBC, renal, ECG per ASA.
VTE: mechanical + LMWH at least 7 days.

patientEducation: Recovery time; no heavy lifting; when to resume intercourse per surgeon's advice.
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking and reduce alcohol before surgery (NICE NG180).
Stay active; prehabilitation exercises where advised.
mdtReferrals: Gynaecology; anaesthetic pre-assessment; haematology if bleeding disorder.
dischargeCriteria: Pain controlled with oral analgesia; eating, drinking and mobilising.
Wound satisfactory; VTE prophylaxis plan and follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Post-operative review per surgical team; return immediately with fever, wound redness, calf swelling, breathlessness or chest pain.
